- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.16) over 3+ days, model underestimates downward trend; add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days); cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 7-day average to avoid lagged bias.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude by 5–10% to reflect sentiment lag.
